words.example: Algorithmic recommendation feeds can inadvertently reinforce existing cognitive biases by isolating users in echo chambers.

words.meaning: khôi phục, phục hồi, tái thiết
words.definition: To return a damaged ecosystem, institution, confidence, or artefact to its former healthy or original condition.
words.example: Coordinated wetland conservation projects aim to restore natural floodplains and revive endangered migratory bird populations.

words.meaning: chỉnh sửa, sửa đổi, xem xét lại
words.definition: To reconsider, alter, or update a text, estimate, curriculum, or policy in light of new information.
words.example: Economists had to revise their annual growth projections downward following unexpected global supply bottlenecks.

words.meaning: lịch trình, kế hoạch thời gian
words.definition: A structured timetable or procedural plan detailing when specific tasks or events are to take place.
words.example: Major public infrastructure projects frequently exceed their original budget and fall behind their projected schedule.

words.definition: Characterised by anxiety, strained relations, or heightened anticipation of conflict.
words.example: Diplomatic negotiations over shared transboundary river basins remained exceptionally tense throughout the drought.

words.meaning: chấm dứt, kết thúc chính thức
words.definition: To bring a contract, agreement, process, or relationship to a formal and definitive end.
words.example: Either contracting party reserves the legal right to terminate the partnership in the event of material breach.

words.meaning: chủ đề xuyên suốt, đề tài chính
words.definition: A recurring central idea, motif, or unifying concept explored in a discourse, work, or conference.
words.example: Intergenerational equity emerged as the overarching theme of the international climate summit.

words.meaning: nhờ đó, qua đó, do vậy
words.definition: By that means, or as a direct logical consequence of the action just mentioned.
words.example: Expanding commuter rail networks reduces private car dependency, thereby lowering urban greenhouse gas emissions.

words.meaning: đồng nhất, đồng đều, nhất quán
words.definition: Remaining consistent and unvarying in form, standard, distribution, or quality across all cases.
words.example: Establishing uniform accounting standards across jurisdictions enhances transparency for international institutional investors.

words.meaning: phương tiện giao thông, công cụ truyền tải
words.definition: A machine used for transporting people or goods, or a medium through which an idea or policy is conveyed.
words.example: Subsidising electric vehicle adoption accelerates the decarbonisation of municipal public transport fleets.

words.meaning: ảo (trực tuyến), gần như thực tế
words.definition: Simulated or carried out via computer networks rather than physically, or being effectively so in practice.
words.example: Virtual laboratory simulations allow underfunded secondary schools to conduct complex chemistry experiments safely.

words.definition: Relating to sight, perception by the eyes, or graphical representation of information.
words.example: Effective visual data presentation enables policymakers to grasp multifaceted demographic shifts at a glance.

words.meaning: đáp ứng, điều chỉnh để phù hợp; cung cấp chỗ ở
words.definition: To adapt to or make space for different needs, demands, or a number of people.
words.example: Urban transport networks must be redesigned to accommodate the rapidly growing commuter population.

words.meaning: phép loại suy, sự tương đồng để so sánh giải thích
words.definition: A comparison between two different things that highlights structural or functional similarities for explanation.
words.example: The lecturer drew a compelling analogy between the human immune system and national cybersecurity defences.

words.meaning: dự đoán trước, lường trước và chuẩn bị ứng phó
words.definition: To foresee a future event or problem and take appropriate action in advance.
words.example: Policymakers failed to anticipate the long-term demographic pressures caused by declining birth rates.

words.meaning: cam đoan, bảo đảm, trấn an
words.definition: To tell someone confidently that something is true or certain, or to make an outcome guaranteed.
words.example: Strict regulatory audits are necessary to assure consumers that organic food labels are genuinely trustworthy.

words.meaning: đạt được, giành được (mục tiêu, trình độ cao)
words.definition: To succeed in achieving a desired standard, goal, or level after sustained effort.
words.example: Equitable funding enables students from underprivileged areas to attain higher academic qualifications.

words.meaning: sự đại diện, lợi ích (thường dùng trong 'on behalf of')
words.definition: The interest, representation, or benefit of a particular person, group, or organisation.
words.example: Environmental NGOs frequently lobby international summits on behalf of vulnerable coastal communities.

words.meaning: phần lớn, đa số; khối lượng lớn
words.definition: The main or largest part of something, or a large physical mass or quantity.
words.example: The bulk of municipal waste in developing megacities still consists of untreated organic matter.

words.definition: To bring or come to a complete end; to stop happening or operating.
words.example: Several heavy manufacturing plants were forced to cease operations after failing environmental inspections.

words.meaning: mạch lạc, logic, gắn kết chặt chẽ
words.definition: Logical, well-organised, and consistent so that parts fit together clearly as a whole.
words.example: Without a coherent national energy strategy, intermittent renewable subsidies yield disappointing results.

words.meaning: trùng hợp (về thời gian, quan điểm hoặc sự kiện)
words.definition: To occur at the same time as another event, or to agree closely in opinion or interest.
words.example: The sharpest decline in print newspaper readership appeared to coincide with the rise of smartphones.

words.meaning: bắt đầu, khởi công, khởi sự (trang trọng)
words.definition: To begin formally or officially, especially a project, legal proceeding, or academic term.
words.example: Construction of the high-speed railway is scheduled to commence following the final ecological review.

words.meaning: tương thích, phù hợp, có thể cùng tồn tại
words.definition: Able to exist, function, or be used together without conflict or technical difficulty.
words.example: Economists increasingly debate whether rapid GDP expansion is truly compatible with planetary ecological limits.

words.meaning: đồng thời, diễn ra cùng lúc
words.definition: Happening, existing, or operating at the exact same time.
words.example: Public hospitals struggled to cope with concurrent outbreaks of seasonal influenza and heat-related illness.

words.meaning: giới hạn, thu hẹp phạm vi; giam giữ
words.definition: To keep or restrict someone or something within specific boundaries, limits, or areas.
words.example: University curricula should not confine students to narrow vocational skills at the expense of critical inquiry.

words.meaning: sự tranh cãi gay gắt, vấn đề gây tranh luận công khai
words.definition: Prolonged public disagreement or heated debate over a sensitive or disputed issue.
words.example: The deployment of automated surveillance cameras in residential neighbourhoods sparked intense public controversy.

words.meaning: điều ngược lại, mệnh đề đảo
words.definition: A statement, situation, or idea that is the exact opposite or reverse of another.
words.example: While wealth can broaden educational access, the converse is not always true for emotional fulfilment.

words.meaning: thiết bị, dụng cụ; thủ pháp (tu từ, kỹ thuật)
words.definition: A piece of mechanical or electronic equipment made for a specific purpose, or a rhetorical technique.
words.example: Constant notifications from handheld devices can severely fragment adolescents' concentration during study.

words.meaning: dành toàn bộ (thời gian, nguồn lực, tâm huyết) cho
words.definition: To give a significant proportion of time, money, or effort to a particular purpose or cause.
words.example: Governments ought to devote a larger share of healthcare budgets to preventive medicine rather than emergency care.

words.meaning: làm giảm bớt, suy giảm (giá trị, tầm quan trọng)
words.definition: To become smaller, weaker, or less important, or to reduce the value or authority of something.
words.example: Over-reliance on machine translation may gradually diminish learners' motivation to master foreign languages.

words.meaning: bóp méo, xuyên tạc, làm sai lệch
words.definition: To twist facts, data, or perceptions out of their true or original state, often misleadingly.
words.example: Selective reporting by partisan media outlets can systematically distort public perceptions of crime rates.

words.meaning: khoảng thời gian tồn tại, thời lượng
words.definition: The length of time during which a process, condition, or event continues.
words.example: Extending the duration of compulsory schooling has been linked to higher lifetime earnings across Europe.

words.meaning: xói mòn; làm suy yếu dần (niềm tin, giá trị)
words.definition: To gradually wear away land, rock, or abstract qualities such as trust, authority, or cultural identity.
words.example: Persistent corporate tax scandals tend to erode citizens' confidence in democratic institutions.

words.meaning: hệ giá trị đạo đức, tinh thần chuẩn mực
words.definition: A set of moral principles guiding the behaviour and values of an individual, profession, or society.
words.example: A strong conservation ethic must be embedded in primary education to cultivate environmentally responsible citizens.

words.meaning: định dạng, cấu trúc trình bày, hình thức tổ chức
words.definition: The specific arrangement, structure, or technical standard in which information or an event is presented.
words.example: Transitioning university examinations to an open-book format encourages analytical reasoning over memorisation.

words.meaning: thành lập, sáng lập; đặt nền móng cho
words.definition: To establish an institution, organisation, or settlement, or to base an argument on a principle.
words.example: Philanthropic coalitions collaborated to found an independent research institute dedicated to clean water.

words.meaning: vốn có, cố hữu, nội tại
words.definition: Existing as a permanent, essential, or inseparable characteristic of something.
words.example: Critics warn that algorithmic recruitment software carries inherent biases inherited from historical hiring data.

words.meaning: cái nhìn sâu sắc, sự thấu hiểu bản chất
words.definition: A deep, clear, and accurate understanding of a complex phenomenon, problem, or human behaviour.
words.example: Archaeological excavations provide invaluable insight into ancient trade networks and urban sanitation.

words.meaning: không thể thiếu, cấu thành thiết yếu
words.definition: Essential and necessary to make a system, process, or whole complete.
words.example: Public libraries remain an integral part of civic life by offering free digital access to low-income residents.

words.meaning: thuộc về tay chân, thủ công (không tự động hóa)
words.definition: Done with the hands or physical effort rather than by automated machinery or electronic systems.
words.example: Advances in industrial robotics are steadily replacing repetitive manual tasks across automotive assembly lines.

words.meaning: trưởng thành, chín chắn; phát triển hoàn chỉnh
words.definition: Fully developed mentally, emotionally, or structurally, showing sound judgement or established stability.
words.example: Solar photovoltaics have evolved into a mature technology capable of undercutting coal-fired power plants.

words.meaning: hòa giải, làm trung gian điều tiết
words.definition: To intervene neutrally between opposing parties to help resolve a dispute or bring about agreement.
words.example: Independent international bodies are often called upon to mediate cross-border water-sharing disputes.

words.meaning: phương tiện truyền tải, môi trường trung gian
words.definition: A channel, system, or material through which information, artistic expression, or effects are conveyed.
words.example: Short-form video has emerged as the dominant medium for political campaigning among younger voters.

words.meaning: thuộc về quân sự, quân đội
words.definition: Relating to armed forces, defence operations, or warfare.
words.example: Many civilian breakthroughs, including GPS and the internet, originated from state-funded military research.

words.meaning: tối thiểu, ở mức nhỏ nhất có thể
words.definition: Of the smallest possible amount, degree, or impact.
words.example: Well-designed eco-resorts aim to leave minimal ecological disturbance on surrounding coral reefs.

words.meaning: lẫn nhau, song phương, cùng chia sẻ
words.definition: Experienced, felt, or done equally by two or more parties toward each other.
words.example: Bilateral trade agreements endure only when both economies perceive tangible mutual benefits.

words.meaning: chuẩn mực xã hội, quy tắc thông lệ
words.definition: An accepted standard, pattern of behaviour, or expectation regarded as typical within a group or society.
words.example: Flexible hybrid schedules have rapidly shifted from an unusual perk to an accepted workplace norm.

words.meaning: chồng chéo, giao thoa, trùng lặp một phần
words.definition: To share common areas, responsibilities, or time periods partially with another entity.
words.example: When municipal and national agencies overlap in jurisdiction, disaster relief efforts can become sluggish.

words.meaning: thụ động, tiếp nhận mà không chủ động tham gia
words.definition: Accepting or allowing what happens without active participation, resistance, or critical engagement.
words.example: Passive consumption of endless social media feeds correlates with reduced attention spans among teenagers.

words.meaning: một phần, khẩu phần, tỷ phần
words.definition: A distinct part or share of a larger whole, budget, population, or serving.
words.example: A substantial portion of household income in major financial capitals is absorbed by housing costs.

words.meaning: sơ bộ, ban đầu, mang tính chuẩn bị
words.definition: Preceding or done in preparation for a fuller, more decisive investigation, negotiation, or action.
words.example: Preliminary clinical findings indicate that the new vaccine significantly lowers hospitalisation rates.

words.meaning: quy trình chuẩn, giao thức, nghị định thư
words.definition: An official system of rules, scientific procedures, or diplomatic conventions governing conduct or operations.
words.example: Hospitals introduced stricter hygiene protocol guidelines to curb the spread of drug-resistant bacteria.

words.meaning: tinh chỉnh, hoàn thiện, lọc tinh
words.definition: To improve an idea, method, or system by making precise incremental changes, or to purify a substance.
words.example: Engineers continuously refine battery chemistry to increase electric vehicle range while lowering costs.

words.meaning: nới lỏng (quy định, kiểm soát); thư giãn
words.definition: To make a rule, restriction, or control less strict, or to become less tense.
words.example: Environmentalists cautioned lawmakers not to relax air-quality regulations during the economic slowdown.

words.meaning: kiềm chế, kìm hãm, ngăn chặn
words.definition: To prevent someone or something from acting excessively or moving beyond controlled limits.
words.example: Central banks raise interest rates primarily to restrain runaway inflation and cool overheated markets.

words.meaning: cuộc cách mạng, sự biến đổi triệt để
words.definition: A dramatic, fundamental transformation in technology, society, economics, or political governance.
words.example: The digital revolution has fundamentally reshaped how citizens access news, education, and public services.

words.meaning: cứng nhắc, thiếu linh hoạt, khắt khe
words.definition: Unable or unwilling to adapt, bend, or change in response to evolving circumstances.
words.example: Excessively rigid standardised curricula often stifle teachers' creativity and disregard individual learning paces.

words.meaning: tuyến đường, lộ trình; con đường đạt mục tiêu
words.definition: A specific path taken from one place to another, or a method for achieving a particular outcome.
words.example: Expanding dedicated bus routes across suburban districts offers a cost-effective remedy for peak-hour congestion.

words.meaning: kịch bản, viễn cảnh giả định
words.definition: A projected sequence of possible future events or conditions used for analysis and planning.
words.example: Climate scientists model a worst-case scenario in which Arctic sea ice vanishes entirely during summer months.

words.meaning: lĩnh vực, phạm vi ảnh hưởng; hình cầu
words.definition: A particular domain of activity, knowledge, social life, or political influence.
words.example: Artificial intelligence is rapidly permeating every sphere of modern commerce, from logistics to diagnostics.

words.meaning: cấp dưới, thứ yếu, phụ thuộc
words.definition: Lower in rank, status, authority, or importance relative to another entity.
words.example: Long-term ecological stability should never be treated as subordinate to short-term quarterly profits.

words.meaning: bổ sung, phụ thêm vào để hoàn thiện
words.definition: To add an extra element or amount to something in order to enhance, strengthen, or complete it.
words.example: Online interactive tutorials can effectively supplement traditional classroom lectures rather than replace them.

words.meaning: đình chỉ, tạm dừng, treo (giấy phép, hoạt động)
words.definition: To temporarily stop an activity, right, or service from continuing for a period of time.
words.example: Aviation regulators decided to suspend all flights over the region until volcanic ash levels subsided.

words.meaning: đội ngũ, nhóm chuyên gia phối hợp
words.definition: A group of individuals working collaboratively toward a shared professional, academic, or athletic objective.
words.example: An interdisciplinary team of epidemiologists and urban designers collaborated to evaluate neighbourhood walkability.

words.meaning: tạm thời, nhất thời, không lâu dài
words.definition: Lasting or intended to function only for a limited period rather than permanently.
words.example: Emergency fuel subsidies offer only temporary relief and fail to address underlying energy inefficiency.

words.meaning: kích hoạt, châm ngòi, gây ra phản ứng dây chuyền
words.definition: To cause an event, reaction, or chain of consequences to happen suddenly.
words.example: Prolonged droughts in major grain-exporting regions can trigger severe global food price spikes.

words.meaning: thống nhất, hợp nhất thành một thể chung
words.definition: To bring separate groups, standards, or elements together into a single cohesive whole.
words.example: International sporting tournaments can temporarily unify diverse populations around a shared sense of pride.

words.meaning: vi phạm (luật pháp, quyền riêng tư, chuẩn mực)
words.definition: To break or fail to comply with a law, formal agreement, ethical standard, or fundamental right.
words.example: Tech corporations face heavy fines whenever their data-harvesting practices violate national privacy statutes.

words.meaning: tầm nhìn chiến lược, viễn kiến; thị lực
words.definition: The ability to plan or imagine the future with wisdom, foresight, and clear strategic purpose.
words.example: Transforming car-centric metropolises into sustainable communities requires bold long-term political vision.

words.meaning: liền kề, tiếp giáp, kế cận
words.definition: Located immediately next to or sharing a common border with something else.
words.example: Heavy industrial zones should never be constructed directly adjacent to primary schools or hospitals.

words.meaning: tập hợp, lắp ráp, thu thập lại
words.definition: To gather people, evidence, or mechanical components together into an organised whole.
words.example: The parliamentary committee had to assemble experts from across the continent before drafting AI legislation.

words.meaning: sụp đổ, tan rã, suy sụp đột ngột
words.definition: To fall down suddenly or fail completely as a structure, system, institution, or ecosystem.
words.example: Marine biologists warn that regional fisheries could collapse within two decades if illegal trawling persists.

words.meaning: biên soạn, tổng hợp (dữ liệu, báo cáo)
words.definition: To collect and systematically organise information from multiple sources into a report, list, or database.
words.example: Researchers took three years to compile a comprehensive longitudinal dataset covering fifty urban districts.

words.meaning: hình thành ý tưởng, thai nghén; hình dung ra
words.definition: To form or devise a plan, idea, or theory in the mind, or to imagine something as possible.
words.example: Urban architects must conceive innovative housing models that remain affordable without sacrificing liveability.

words.meaning: thuyết phục hoàn toàn (khiến ai tin hoặc đồng thuận)
words.definition: To persuade someone firmly to believe a claim or adopt a particular course of action through evidence or argument.
words.example: Transparent empirical evidence is essential to convince sceptical motorists to switch to public transit.

words.meaning: làm suy giảm, kéo tụt (kinh tế, giá trị); gây trầm cảm
words.definition: To reduce the level, value, or activity of an economy or market, or to lower someone's mood.
words.example: Excessive household debt tends to depress consumer demand and prolong post-recession recovery.

words.meaning: đối mặt, gặp phải (khó khăn, trở ngại, hiện tượng)
words.definition: To unexpectedly experience or be confronted with a challenge, obstacle, or unfamiliar situation.
words.example: First-generation university graduates often encounter structural barriers when entering elite corporate professions.

words.meaning: khổng lồ, to lớn, cực kỳ đáng kể
words.definition: Extremely large in scale, amount, impact, or significance.
words.example: Decarbonising global aviation presents an enormous engineering challenge that cannot be solved overnight.

words.meaning: sắp tới, sắp diễn ra; sẵn lòng cung cấp thông tin
words.definition: About to happen, be published, or become available soon; willing to share information openly.
words.example: The forthcoming international climate summit will determine binding emission targets for the next decade.

words.meaning: có khuynh hướng, thiên về, nghiêng về
words.definition: To feel willing or disposed toward a particular belief, opinion, or course of action.
words.example: Recent consumer surveys incline economists to believe that green products require stronger price incentives.

words.meaning: nội tại, bản chất vốn có, tự thân
words.definition: Belonging naturally and essentially to the core nature of something, independent of external factors.
words.example: Preserving endangered wildlife has intrinsic ecological value beyond its measurable contribution to ecotourism.

words.meaning: viện dẫn (luật, nguyên tắc); khơi gợi
words.definition: To cite a law, authority, or principle as justification for an action, or to evoke a strong response.
words.example: Several municipalities had to invoke emergency powers to ration drinking water during the historic drought.

words.meaning: đánh thuế, áp đặt khoản thu bắt buộc
words.definition: To impose and officially collect a tax, fee, or financial charge by legal authority.
words.example: Several European capitals now levy additional congestion charges on older diesel vehicles entering downtown zones.

words.meaning: tương tự như vậy, cũng thế
words.definition: In the same manner or to a similar extent; also.
words.example: Air pollution damages respiratory health; likewise, prolonged exposure to urban noise elevates cardiovascular risk.

words.meaning: tuy nhiên, dẫu vậy, mặc dù thế
words.definition: In spite of what has just been mentioned or conceded; nevertheless.
words.example: Remote education lacks spontaneous peer interaction; nonetheless, it expands university access for rural learners.

words.definition: Different from what is expected or usual; not divisible by two, or occasional.
words.example: Auditors noticed several odd statistical discrepancies in the corporation's annual carbon-offset disclosures.

words.meaning: đang diễn ra, liên tục, kéo dài
words.definition: Continuing to exist, develop, or happen without interruption.
words.example: Ongoing investment in teacher professional development is vital to sustain gains in national literacy.

words.meaning: hội đồng chuyên gia, ban thẩm định; tấm bảng
words.definition: A small group of qualified individuals selected to discuss, advise on, or judge an official matter.
words.example: An independent panel of bioethicists was appointed to review clinical protocols for human genome editing.

words.meaning: dai dẳng, tiếp diễn; kiên trì bám đuổi
words.definition: To continue to exist or occur despite opposition, difficulty, or corrective measures.
words.example: Despite decades of equal-pay legislation, stark gender disparities still persist in executive leadership.

words.meaning: đặt ra (thách thức, nguy cơ, câu hỏi)
words.definition: To present or constitute a problem, threat, danger, or question requiring serious consideration.
words.example: Unregulated deepfake audio tools pose a serious threat to electoral integrity and public journalism.

words.meaning: miễn cưỡng, do dự, không sẵn lòng
words.definition: Unwilling and hesitant to take a particular action or accept a change.
words.example: Small manufacturers are often reluctant to adopt costly green technologies without guaranteed tax credits.

words.meaning: cái gọi là (thường hàm ý hoài nghi hoặc mỉa mai)
words.definition: Commonly named in a certain way, often used to express scepticism about the label's accuracy.
words.example: Many so-called biodegradable plastics actually require industrial composting facilities to break down safely.

words.meaning: đơn giản, rõ ràng, dễ hiểu, trực diện
words.definition: Uncomplicated, clear, and easy to understand or carry out.
words.example: Designing a fair carbon pricing system is far less straightforward than proponents initially suggested.

words.meaning: nhờ đó, theo đó, bằng cách mà
words.definition: By which or through which a system, process, or formal arrangement operates.
words.example: The city introduced a congestion scheme whereby all toll revenues directly fund electric bus fleets.

words.definition: to distribute resources, funds, or duties for a specific purpose
words.example: Governments should allocate more funding to primary education.

words.meaning: có tầm ảnh hưởng sâu rộng
words.definition: having important and widely applicable effects or implications
words.example: This trend is likely to have far-reaching implications for society as a whole.

words.definition: a room, building, or place in which someone may live or stay
words.example: Finding affordable student accommodation near university campuses has become increasingly challenging.

words.definition: a set of written questions used for gathering statistical or survey data
words.example: Researchers distributed an anonymous questionnaire to over five hundred local residents.

words.meaning: bài tập lớn, nhiệm vụ được giao
words.definition: a piece of work or task allocated to someone as part of a course or job
words.example: University students must submit their written assignment before the Friday deadline.

words.meaning: buổi học hướng dẫn nhóm nhỏ
words.definition: a period of intensive tuition given by a university tutor to an individual or small group
words.example: Each weekly tutorial allows undergraduates to discuss complex readings with their lecturer.

words.definition: a conference or university class for discussion and academic training on a specific topic
words.example: Postgraduate scholars presented their preliminary findings at the international seminar.

words.definition: a half-year term in a school or university academic calendar
words.example: Exchange students typically spend one full semester studying at a partner institution abroad.

words.meaning: luận văn, luận án học thuật
words.definition: a long, formal essay on a particular subject written for a university degree
words.example: She spent an entire year conducting field research for her doctoral dissertation.

words.meaning: danh mục tài liệu tham khảo
words.definition: a systematic list of books and scholarly sources referred to in an academic work
words.example: Every academic paper must include an accurate bibliography formatted according to citation rules.

words.meaning: thời khóa biểu, lịch trình cố định
words.definition: a structured schedule showing the times at which classes, trains, or events occur
words.example: A well-balanced school timetable should allocate adequate hours to both arts and sciences.

words.meaning: sự đăng ký nhập học, sĩ số ghi danh
words.definition: the action of officially registering as a member of an institution or course
words.example: University enrolment in computer science courses has surged dramatically over the past decade.

words.meaning: chính phủ, cơ quan cầm quyền
words.definition: the governing body of a nation, state, or community with authority to enact policies
words.example: The central government introduced stricter emissions targets to combat urban air pollution.

words.definition: an institution where objects of historical, scientific, or artistic interest are preserved and exhibited
words.example: Free admission to national museum collections encourages greater public engagement with history.

words.meaning: nhà thờ chính tòa, giáo đường lớn

words.meaning: vượt trên cả, bên cạnh những yếu tố đã nêu
words.definition: In addition to or exceeding what has already been stated, expected, or required.
words.example: Over and above immediate tuition costs, postgraduate students frequently struggle with soaring urban housing rents.

words.meaning: gắn kết chặt chẽ không thể tách rời
words.definition: So closely intertwined and mutually dependent that one factor cannot be separated from or analysed without the other.
words.example: Public health experts emphasise that childhood nutrition and long-term educational attainment are inextricably linked.

words.meaning: loại trừ lẫn nhau, không thể cùng tồn tại
words.definition: Unable to exist, occur, or be achieved simultaneously because the presence of one precludes the other.
words.example: Sustainable industrial growth and stringent environmental protection need not be treated as mutually exclusive objectives.

words.meaning: tương đương với, chẳng khác nào (thường mang nghĩa tiêu cực)
words.definition: Equivalent in seriousness, effect, or moral weight to another typically undesirable act or condition.
words.example: Ignoring verified safety warnings from site engineers was tantamount to gross negligence in the eyes of the tribunal.

words.meaning: con dao hai lưỡi (vừa lợi vừa hại)
words.definition: A development, technology, or policy that simultaneously brings substantial benefits and serious adverse consequences.
words.example: Generative automation represents a double-edged sword, boosting administrative efficiency while displacing entry-level clerical roles.

words.meaning: thời khắc bước ngoặt mang tính lịch sử
words.definition: A decisive turning point marking a profound, irreversible shift in history, policy, science, or cultural attitudes.
words.example: The ratification of the global climate accord marked a watershed moment in international environmental diplomacy.

words.meaning: vòng luẩn quẩn tiêu cực tự khuếch đại
words.definition: A self-reinforcing chain of adverse events in which each problem intensifies the next, making escape increasingly difficult.
words.example: Underfunded public transit triggers declining ridership and falling revenues, trapping municipal operators in a vicious circle.

words.meaning: phần nổi của tảng băng chìm
words.definition: A small, immediately visible fraction of a much larger, hidden, and more complex underlying problem.
collocations: merely the tip of the iceberg
just the tip of the iceberg
represent the tip of the iceberg
words.example: Reported incidents of online financial fraud represent merely the tip of the iceberg, as many elderly victims never file complaints.
synonyms: small part of a wider issue

words.meaning: tâm điểm tranh cãi, vấn đề gây bất đồng sâu sắc
words.definition: A persistent subject or issue over which opposing parties strongly disagree and repeatedly argue.
words.example: Allocating water rights along transboundary rivers remains a recurring bone of contention between upstream and downstream nations.

words.meaning: gánh chịu hậu quả hoặc tác động nặng nề nhất
words.definition: To endure the worst impact, greatest hardship, or primary burden of an adverse event or policy change.
words.example: Low-income coastal households invariably bear the brunt of rising flood insurance premiums and extreme storm surges.

words.meaning: mở đường, tạo tiền đề thuận lợi cho bước tiến mới
words.definition: To create the necessary conditions, framework, or groundwork enabling a subsequent breakthrough or reform to occur.
words.example: Standardised cross-border data rules can pave the way for collaborative medical research across European hospitals.

words.meaning: làm sáng tỏ, soi chiếu bản chất vấn đề
words.definition: To clarify, explain, or reveal fresh evidence regarding a complex, obscure, or previously misunderstood topic.
words.example: Longitudinal household surveys shed light on how early childhood reading habits shape adult economic mobility.

words.meaning: ngăn chặn đà gia tăng, kìm hãm xu hướng tiêu cực
words.definition: To halt, slow down, or reverse the rapid growth of an undesirable trend or widespread crisis.
words.example: Targeted rural broadband investment and local grants are helping small towns stem the tide of youth depopulation.

words.meaning: thiết lập sự cân bằng hài hòa giữa hai yếu tố đối lập
words.definition: To reach a fair, workable compromise between two competing priorities, interests, or extremes.
words.example: Regulators must strike a balance between fostering technological innovation and safeguarding citizens' personal privacy.
